 13: Yeats said that the poem "is founded upon some things a fisherman said to
me when out fishing in Sligo Bay."
 14: Yeats explained that Father O'Hart (d. 1739) "was greatly beloved. These
lines accurately record the tradition. No one who has held the stolen land has
prospered. It has changed owners many times." In another note he cited his
source, T. O'Rorke, History, Antiquities, and Present State of the Parishes of Bal-
lysadare and Kilvamet, in the County of Sligo (1878).
 14.2: the penal laws against Roman Catholics were enacted from 1695-1727.
 Some Catholics evaded the law against owning landed property by giving
nominal possession of their holdings to Protestants.
